Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2026-34926 Trend Micro Apex One On-Premise Server fleet exposure surveillance
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Trend Micro Apex One agent service spawning LOLBin/script-interpreter children (CVE-2026-34926 post-exploit fleet-poisoning symptom)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] CVE-2026-34926 Trend Micro Apex One On-Premise Server fleet exposure surveillance Exploitation High
Inventory all Windows hosts in TVM/vulnerability data reporting exposure to CVE-2026-34926 (Apex One on-premise directory traversal). Because exploitation requires admin access to the Apex One server and TrendAI has already observed in-the-wild attempts, every unpatched server is on a 14-day federal CISA KEV clock (deadline 2026-06-04). The detection isn't behavioural — it's a posture pivot that tells the SOC exactly which servers to wrap with the behavioural UC below until they're patched to SP1 CP Build 18012 or SP1 Build 17079. Rationale: The CVE ID itself (CVE-2026-34926) is the highest-fidelity string in the article — it maps cleanly to a single row in vulnerability inventory tables. Cross-checked vendor bulletin KA-0023430 for fixed builds (SP1 CP Build 18012 / SP1 Build 17079) and CISA KEV catalog for the 2026-06-04 federal remediation deadline, both confirming the CVE is in-scope. Cross-checked against: • https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0023430 • https://www.securityweek.com/trendai-patches-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/ • https://www.jpcert.or.jp/english/at/2026/at260014.html • https://www.hkcert.org/security-bulletin/trend-micro-apex-one-multiple-vulnerabilities_20260522

[LLM] Trend Micro Apex One agent service spawning LOLBin/script-interpreter children (CVE-2026-34926 post-exploit fleet-poisoning symptom) Installation Medium
The article specifically describes the exploitation outcome as 'inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations' — i.e. the Apex One server pushes attacker-controlled code which executes under the agent service context on every managed endpoint. This hunt targets the symptom on the agent fleet: Apex One agent service binaries (PccNTMon.exe, TmListen.exe, NTRtScan.exe, TmCCSF.exe, OfcDog.exe and the Trend service-host family) spawning interpreters / LOLBins that the agent has no legitimate reason to invoke. Scope tightly to the disclosure window (2026-05-21 onward) and to fleets managed by any unpatched on-prem Apex One server surfaced by UC#1. Rationale: Anchored to the article's explicit exploitation outcome: 'inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations'. The parent-process list (PccNTMon, TmListen, NTRtScan, TmCCSF, etc.) is publicly-documented Apex One agent service inventory from Trend Micro product documentation, and a Trend Micro signed service spawning LOLBins is genuinely anomalous behaviour. Filter on InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName='Trend Micro' confirms we're hitting the real agent and not an impersonator. The 2026-05-21 cutoff bounds the hunt to the disclosure window for CISA KEV (KEV add date). Cross-checked against: • https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0023430 • https://www.securityweek.com/trendai-patches-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/ • https://securityaffairs.com/192529/hacking/u-s-cisa-adds-trend-micro-apex-one-and-langflow-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html

title: Trend Micro Apex One Agent Spawning LOLBin or Script Interpreter
id: 9a2f3d4e-8b1c-4f6d-a5e7-2c1b4d9e8f7a
description: Detects Apex One agent service binaries spawning interpreters or LOLBins. Following CVE-2026-34926 (directory traversal in Apex One on-premise server allowing attackers with server-admin credentials to inject code that the server then deploys to all managed agents), this parent-child relationship is the fleet-wide post-exploitation symptom on endpoints.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/trend-micro-warns-of-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-attacks/
  - https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0023430
  - https://www.securityweek.com/trendai-patches-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1574
  - attack.t1072
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\pccntmon.exe'
      - '\tmlisten.exe'
      - '\ntrtscan.exe'
      - '\tmccsf.exe'
      - '\tmccscanservice.exe'
      - '\tmbmsrv.exe'
      - '\ofcdog.exe'
      - '\coreserviceshell.exe'
      - '\coreframeworkhost.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
      - '\installutil.exe'
      - '\hh.exe'
  filter_known_good:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Trend Micro\'
      - '\Apex Central\'
      - 'CTPRetrieve'
      - 'VsapiPS'
  condition: (selection_parent and selection_child) and not filter_known_good
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @ParentImage:(*\pccntmon.exe OR *\PccNTMon.exe OR *\tmlisten.exe OR *\TmListen.exe OR *\ntrtscan.exe OR *\NTRtScan.exe OR *\tmccsf.exe OR *\TmCCSF.exe OR *\tmccscanservice.exe OR *\TmCCSCanService.exe OR *\tmbmsrv.exe OR *\TmBMSrv.exe OR *\ofcdog.exe OR *\OfcDog.exe OR *\coreserviceshell.exe OR *\CoreServiceShell.exe) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msbuild.exe OR *\installutil.exe OR *\hh.exe) -@CommandLine:(*"Trend Micro"* OR *"Apex Central"* OR *CTPRetrieve* OR *VsapiPS*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(pccntmon|tmlisten|ntrtscan|tmccsf|tmccscanservice|tmbmsrv|ofcdog|coreserviceshell|coreframeworkhost)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msbuild|installutil|hh)\.exe$/i
| NOT (regex("\\\\Trend Micro\\\\", field=CommandLine) OR regex("\\\\Apex Central\\\\", field=CommandLine) OR regex("CTPRetrieve", field=CommandLine) OR regex("VsapiPS", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34926")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34926")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated SQLi probe against Drupal endpoints (CVE-2026-9082) · [LLM] Drupal/PHP/web server process spawning shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-9082 RCE)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web server writes PHP/PHAR file outside Drupal's compiled-twig path (webshell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Unauthenticated SQLi probe against Drupal endpoints (CVE-2026-9082) Exploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests that target known Drupal API/render endpoints with PHP array-key injection markers or PostgreSQL-specific SQLi syntax characteristic of CVE-2026-9082 EntityQuery condition handler abuse. Article-specific because the flaw is reached via crafted array keys passed to the database abstraction API, leaving telltale `[...']`, `pg_sleep`, `pg_read_file`, or `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` tokens in URLs/POST bodies on Drupal paths. Rationale: Anchored on the article-confirmed root cause (PHP array-key injection reaching the PostgreSQL EntityQuery condition handler) and the Searchlight Cyber PoC writeup describing anonymous SQLi via crafted bracket/quote keys; PostgreSQL-only RCE primitives (`COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`, `pg_read_file`, `lo_import`) are unique enough to be high-fidelity if seen in a Drupal URL. Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/highly-critical-drupal-core-flaw.html • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2026-9082-highly-critical-sql-injection-vulnerability-in-drupal-core-sa-core-2026-004
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let DrupalPaths = dynamic(["/jsonapi/","/node/","/views/ajax","/search/","/rest/","/entity/","/user/login","/?q="]);
let SqliMarkers = dynamic(["pg_sleep","UNION SELECT","union select","COPY FROM PROGRAM","pg_read_file","lo_import","%5B%27","%27%5D","' OR '","')--","--+"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where csUriStem has_any (DrupalPaths)
    | where (csUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers)) or (csUriQuery has "[" and csUriQuery has "'")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, Host=Computer, Url=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UA=csUserAgent, Src="IIS"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url has_any (DrupalPaths)
    | where Url has_any (SqliMarkers) or (Url has "[" and Url has "'")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Host=DstHostname, Url, Method=HttpMethod, Status=HttpStatusCode, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Src="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Drupal/PHP/web server process spawning shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-9082 RCE) Exploitation High
Detects classic web-to-shell post-exploitation where php-fpm/apache/nginx/IIS w3wp (the typical Drupal runtimes) parents a shell, LOLBin, or reverse-shell one-liner. This is the highest-fidelity host-side signal that the SQLi described in the article has been escalated to RCE via Drupal's PostgreSQL backend. Rationale: Drupal sites run under php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp; the article explicitly states CVE-2026-9082 can yield RCE on PostgreSQL backends. Web-server parent + shell/LOLBin child is the canonical post-RCE pivot — high-confidence even without a specific payload string, because Drupal's runtime almost never legitimately spawns /bin/sh, nc, or PowerShell encoded commands. Cross-checked against Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004 and Searchlight Cyber PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/highly-critical-drupal-core-flaw.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

let ShellChildren = dynamic(["sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","socat","whoami","id","uname","hostname"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebParents)
| where FileName in~ (ShellChildren)
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","sh -i","nc -e","mkfifo","python -c","perl -e","-NoProfile -enc","-NoP -e","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl http","wget http")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| extend ParentBase = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ParentProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))
| extend ChildBase  = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ActingProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Web server writes PHP/PHAR file outside Drupal's compiled-twig path (webshell drop) Installation High
Detects php-fpm/apache/nginx/IIS w3wp creating .php/.phtml/.phar/.inc files in locations other than Drupal's known compiled-template cache. Article-specific because CVE-2026-9082's RCE primitive on PostgreSQL (via `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` or PHP write through file-include chains) typically lands as a webshell in the document root or `sites/default/files/`. Rationale: Drupal's only legitimate PHP-write path at runtime is the compiled twig cache under `sites/default/files/php/twig/`; anything else written by the PHP runtime is highly suspect. The article + Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004 confirm RCE is possible on PostgreSQL backends, and webshells in `sites/default/files/` are the textbook post-exploitation artefact for Drupal compromises (consistent with prior Drupalgeddon campaigns). Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/

let WebParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebParents)
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where not(FolderPath has_any ("files/php/twig","files\\php\\twig","core/lib","core\\lib","/vendor/","\\vendor\\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

let WebParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php"]);

| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend ProcBase = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ActingProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))
| where ProcBase in (WebParents)
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","inc")

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-9082")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-9082")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

[LLM] MiniUpdate UpdateChecker.dll sideload via legitimate signed .NET host Installation High
Detects loading of the Screening Serpens MiniUpdate payload (internal name UpdateChecker.dll) by a legitimate signed .NET host process via DLL sideloading. The DLL is dropped alongside a hijack-vulnerable benign binary from the Hiring Portal.zip lure and loaded from non-standard user-writable directories. Rationale: Pivots on Unit 42's named internal DLL `UpdateChecker.dll` plus the eight published SHA256 hashes for the MiniUpdate RAT family. User-writable path filter mirrors Screening Serpens' Hiring Portal.zip ZIP-extract sideload chain. Cross-checked against Check Point's 2025 UNC1549 report and MITRE T1574.014 (AppDomainManager Injection). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.014

[LLM] Screening Serpens AppDomainManager hijack via .NET app .config tampering Installation High
Detects writes of a .NET application configuration file (appname.exe.config) containing an `appDomainManagerAssembly` / `appDomainManagerType` entry that redirects CLR initialization to a sideloaded assembly. This is the core Screening Serpens 2026 evolution that disables target app security and loads MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 RATs. Rationale: Targets the specific Unit 42-described evolution: AppDomainManager hijacking that manipulates .NET initialization via a legitimate .config file. The pattern of a same-directory triple (legitimate signed EXE + attacker EXE.config + attacker DLL) in user-writable paths is highly specific to this campaign and rarely seen in legitimate software, which always installs to Program Files via MSI/trusted installers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/ • https://pentestlab.blog/2020/05/20/persistence-appdomainmanager/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1574.002

[LLM] Screening Serpens C2 — DNS/network to UNC1549 infrastructure (Feb-Apr 2026) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or network connection to the four Unit 42-published Screening Serpens C2 domains used during the Feb-Apr 2026 espionage campaign against US, Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern targets. These domains are dedicated per-target/per-variant and seeing any single resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the Unit 42 article as Screening Serpens C2 infrastructure for the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign. The note `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (deliberate typosquat of `business-central-transportation`) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` are highly unusual lures unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Cross-checked against MITRE G1019 (UNC1549) and Check Point's earlier Western Europe expansion report. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

[LLM] Screening Serpens recruitment lure — Hiring Portal.zip + job requisition PDFs Delivery High
Detects delivery of the Screening Serpens spear-phishing lure: an archive named Hiring Portal.zip (or nested within an outer ZIP) accompanied by job-requisition PDFs following the pattern '*Software Engineer*Job ID JR######*.pdf'. Targets technical personnel in aerospace, defense and telecom sectors. Rationale: Pivots on the specific lure filename `Hiring Portal.zip` named by Unit 42 (and previously by Check Point research as a Screening Serpens artifact), plus the documented job-requisition PDF pattern (e.g., `Senior Software Engineer Job ID JR205894.pdf`). Restricting to user-download locations cuts the FP rate from generic HR keyword matches on email gateways. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Filesystem
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
let email = EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName in~ (lureFileNames) or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Software Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Senior.*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation;
let host = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FileName in~ (lureFileNames)) or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl;
union email, host
| order by Timestamp desc
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (lureFileNames) or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Screening Serpens Hiring Portal Lure Archive
id: 4b8c2e15-d6f3-4e1a-9a7c-5e2f8b3d917a
description: Detects creation of the Hiring Portal.zip archive used as the Screening Serpens (UNC1549) MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 spear-phishing lure (Unit 42, May 2026).
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:

  - attack.t1204.002

#event_simpleName=FileWritten

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable UniFi OS devices exposed to CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Vulnerable UniFi OS devices exposed to CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911 Weaponization High
Surfaces managed UniFi OS / UDM / UNVR / UNAS / UCG assets carrying any of the five May-2026 critical CVEs (three CVSS 10.0 plus the additional critical command-injection and information-disclosure flaws). Article-specific because all five CVE IDs are unique to this Ubiquiti advisory bundle; pivots straight from threat-intel to assets that still need patching. Rationale: All seven CVE IDs come directly from the Bleeping Computer article (CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910 plus CVE-2026-33000/34911 patched the same week, and CVE-2026-22557/22558 from the March bundle). Cross-checked against securityonline.info, stack.watch and TheHackerWire for affected SKUs (UDM/UDM-Pro/UDM-SE/UDM-Pro-Max < 5.1.12, UniFi OS Server < 5.0.8, UCG/UNVR/UNAS) which informed the SoftwareName allowlist. Censys reported ~100K internet-exposed UniFi endpoints, so IsInternetFacing is the priority pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/ubiquiti-unifi-os-critical-vulnerabilities-cvss-10-firmware-update/ • https://stack.watch/vuln/CVE-2026-34909/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34908 • https://www.scworld.com/brief/ubiquiti-patches-three-critical-vulnerabilities-in-unifi-os

[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD C2 beacon to 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 endpoint (216.126.225.129:8443) used to exfiltrate CI secrets, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens, and source-code secrets harvested by base64-encoded bash payloads injected into GitHub Actions workflows. Catches both self-hosted runners executing the poisoned workflow and any developer workstation that cloned and ran a compromised pipeline. Rationale: C2 IP 216.126.225.129:8443 is named verbatim in SafeDep's primary write-up and reproduced in cross-coverage from cybersecuritynews.com, cybernews.com, hackread.com — a stable, single-purpose exfil endpoint. Any successful TCP connect to that pair from org telemetry is high-confidence compromise; no legitimate service known at that destination. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/megalodon-malware-github-repos/ • https://hackread.com/github-repositories-megalodon-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1567

| where RemotePort == 8443

        | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcHostname)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Polymarket npm wallet drainer egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev Actions on Objectives High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev — the Cloudflare Worker endpoint used by the nine malicious polymarketdev npm packages (polymarket-trading-cli, polymarket-bot, polymarket-claude-code, etc.) to receive Ethereum/Polygon private keys pasted into the fake postinstall onboarding prompt. Path /v1/wallets/keys is the receive endpoint. Rationale: Domain `polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev` and the receive path `/v1/wallets/keys` are both stated verbatim in SafeDep's report and reproduced by StepSecurity's separate investigation of the polymarketdev/dev-protocol GitHub org takeover. Cloudflare Workers subdomains under a single throwaway account are single-purpose — any DNS hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys

[LLM] Polymarket npm persistence: ~/.polybot/ directory written by node/npm Installation High
Detects creation of files under the ~/.polybot/ persistence directory by node or npm processes. The malicious polymarketdev packages create this directory on first install to drop a device-fingerprint file that allows the operator to track victims across sessions, even before the user pastes a private key. Catches infections that fired but where the C2 egress was blocked or not yet observed. Rationale: SafeDep's polymarket write-up names `~/.polybot/` as the persistence + device-fingerprint directory created by the postinstall hook before the user even sees the wallet prompt; the directory name does not collide with any known legitimate Node tool. Pairing the path with node/npm/npx parent process keeps the rule from firing on coincidental directory names. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/
ATT&CKT1547 T1546.016 T1083

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256

[LLM] Megalodon CI runner: shell scraping /proc/*/environ for in-memory secrets Installation Medium
Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ — the credential-harvesting fingerprint used by the Megalodon GitHub Actions payload to scrape every running process's environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, Vault tokens, etc.) on a self-hosted runner. The article explicitly states the payload reads `/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment` — a behaviour vanishingly rare in legitimate CI workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly lists "/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment" as one of the first data classes the Megalodon harvester collects — that's a unique behavioural string we can pivot on. Combining `/proc/*/environ` access with shell/coreutils parents distinguishes the attack from a developer running `cat /proc/$$/environ` once for debugging. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybernews.com/security/megalodon-github-5000-repos-backdooring-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083 T1057 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings", "head", "tail")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
    or TargetProcessName has_any ("cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Megalodon CI Runner /proc/*/environ Mass Secret Scrape
id: cd4e5f6a-7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a
description: Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ on Linux — the credential-harvesting pattern named in the Megalodon CI/CD payload that scrapes every running process's environment block for CI secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, and OIDC tokens injected by GitHub Actions. Legitimate use of /proc/*/environ from a shell is rare outside debugging or forensic tools.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/megalodon-github-attack-targets-5561.html
  - https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/
author: Detection Team
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
      - '/awk'
      - '/find'
      - '/xargs'
      - '/tr'
      - '/strings'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / DFIR triage tooling intentionally enumerating process environments
  - Performance diagnostics scripts inspecting a single PID's environ (lower /proc cardinality)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*/proc/*/environ* OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/cat OR /bin/cat OR /usr/bin/grep OR /usr/bin/awk OR /usr/bin/find OR /usr/bin/xargs OR /usr/bin/strings)) AND @process.command_line:*environ*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/proc\/[^\s\/]+\/environ/
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|cat|grep|awk|find|xargs|tr|strings|head|tail)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("216.126.225.129") or RemoteUrl has_any ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["216.126.225.129"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("216.126.225.129")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 8 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

1 Introduction This article provides a technical analysis of how many Windows kernel mode drivers can be interacted with from user mode without the hardware they were developed for. This work was motivated by driver-oriented vulnerability research and the need to evaluate the exploitability of individual findings, which frequently affect code whose reachability is hardware-gated. [LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation Installation High
Detects the exact two-step BYOVD deployment sequence the article calls out: `sc.exe create <name> type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` followed by `sc.exe start <name>` on the same host. Sharpens the canonical SigmaHQ kernel-driver rule by requiring the start-follow-up + a .sys binPath ending, eliminating sysadmin driver-install noise. Rationale: Anchored on the article's literal deployment command (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` + `sc.exe start <name>`). The temporal correlation between create+start within 10min on the same service name is what differentiates BYOVD operator behaviour from a sysadmin reading docs. Cross-checked SigmaHQ `proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml` and confirmed the canonical rule does NOT correlate the start follow-up — that's the value-add here. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/ • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/what-are-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-byovd-attacks
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1543.003

let Starts = DeviceProcessEvents

Creates

| where StartTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)

    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"

[LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process Installation Medium
Detects the registry artefact of any BYOVD service install — a new value under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\` where `Type=0x1` (kernel driver) and `ImagePath` references a .sys outside the protected DriverStore. Catches BYOVD frameworks that bypass sc.exe and write the registry directly (CreateServiceW / advapi32). Rationale: Article §3.1 names the registry-and-service install pattern (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel ... binPath= System32\drivers\X.sys`) as the BYOVD prerequisite, and the registry artefact persists even when attackers skip sc.exe entirely (calling CreateServiceW directly). Sysmon EID 13 captures both `Type` and `ImagePath` writes; pairing them on the same service name + filtering DriverStore + TrustedInstaller eliminates Windows Update / OEM driver noise. Cross-checked against CrowdStrike's Scattered Spider BYOVD writeup which lists the same registry hive as the canonical pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
let TypeWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "Type"
    | where RegistryValueData in ("1","0x1","0x00000001")
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project TypeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SvcName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let ImageWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "ImagePath"
    | where RegistryValueData has ".sys"
    | where RegistryValueData !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project ImageTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SvcName, ImagePath = RegistryValueData;
TypeWrites
| join kind=inner ImageWrites on DeviceId, SvcName
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","services.exe","setup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project TypeTime, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SvcName, ImagePath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TypeTime desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 13
| extend ed = parse_xml(EventData)
| extend TargetObject = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[3].["#text"])
| extend Details = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[4].["#text"])
| extend ImageProc = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[5].["#text"])
| where TargetObject matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\(Type|ImagePath)$"
| extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)\\Services\\([^\\]+)\\", 1, TargetObject)
| extend Field = extract(@"(?i)\\([^\\]+)$", 1, TargetObject)
| summarize TypeVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "Type"), ImageVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "ImagePath"), Proc = any(ImageProc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by Computer, SvcName
| where TypeVal in ("1","0x1","DWORD (0x00000001)") and ImageVal has ".sys"
| where ImageVal !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where Proc !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\services.exe"
| project FirstSeen, Computer, SvcName, ImageVal, Proc
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: New Kernel-Type Service Registered with Non-DriverStore .sys ImagePath
id: 8f3c7d22-ba1e-4e7e-9a45-3f7b1d4f9d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Windows service registry key with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) whose ImagePath references a .sys file outside the protected DriverStore. Used by BYOVD frameworks that drop a vulnerable driver and register it as a kernel service for IRP reachability.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_type:
    TargetObject|re: '(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\Type$'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '0x00000001'
      - '0x1'
      - '1'
  filter_trusted:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
  condition: selection_type and not filter_trusted
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate signed third-party driver installation (printer, GPU, VPN, AV)
  - Endpoint management tooling (SCCM/Intune) deploying drivers via custom scripts
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Services\\*\\Type OR *\\Services\\*\\ImagePath OR *\\services\\*\\type OR *\\services\\*\\imagepath) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MSIEXEC.exe OR *\\services.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\Services\\[^\\]+$/i (RegValueName=/^Type$/i OR RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i)
| case {
    RegValueName=/^Type$/i RegStringValue=/^(1|0x0*1)$/ | KernelType:="true";
    RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i RegStringValue=/\.sys/i NOT RegStringValue=/\\DriverStore\\/i | HasDriverPath:="true";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName], function={ collect([RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName, KernelType, HasDriverPath]) })
| KernelType="true" HasDriverPath="true"
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|services)\.exe$/i
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
[LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process Delivery Medium
Detects the BYOVD file-staging step: a .sys file written into `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\` (the canonical binPath target in the article's deployment command) by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, Windows Update or the DriverStore. Pre-stages the alert before the sc.exe service-create fires, giving SOC a chance to catch the drop pre-load. Rationale: Article §3.1 deployment command names `System32\drivers\<x>.sys` as the binPath target. Any .sys landing there from a non-installer process is the pre-load BYOVD staging step. SHA256 from this hit feeds straight into a loldrivers.io / Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist lookup. Filtering DriverStore/WinSxS/TrustedInstaller is what makes this rule production-viable rather than dashboard noise — confirmed against Splunk's published guidance on driver-write monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html • https://reversingops.com/posts/detecting-driver-loading-techniques/ • https://loldrivers.io/
ATT&CKT1068 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\?$"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","drvinst.exe","wuauclt.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\DriverStore\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, SHA256, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\drvinst.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\wuauclt.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\DismHost.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$" and ActorUsername !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Driver File Dropped to System32 Drivers Directory by User Context
id: 1b2e9c44-7c84-4ad1-a3e8-04a0fbc63bea
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a .sys file in C:\Windows\System32\drivers by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, drvinst, or the Windows Update stack. Article-anchored on the BYOVD deployment target path documented by Atos research.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://loldrivers.io/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$'
  filter_installers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
      - '\DismHost.exe'
      - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
  filter_driverstore:
    Image|contains: '\System32\DriverStore\'
  filter_winsxs:
    Image|contains: '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
falsepositives:
  - Vendor MSI installers that bypass DrvInst
  - In-place Windows feature upgrade staging
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\System32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\system32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\SYSTEM32\\DRIVERS\\*.sys) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\drvinst.exe OR *\\DrvInst.exe OR *\\wuauclt.exe OR *\\DismHost.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|drvinst|wuauclt|DismHost|MoUsoCoreWorker)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\System32\\DriverStore\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\Windows\\WinSxS\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\drivers\\*" Filesystem.file_name="*.sys" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT proc_path IN ("*\\TrustedInstaller.exe","*\\msiexec.exe","*\\drvinst.exe","*\\wuauclt.exe","*\\System32\\svchost.exe") | search NOT user IN ("*$","SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, file_name, file_hash, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\drivers\\*" Filesystem.file_name="*.sys" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT proc_path IN ("*\\TrustedInstaller.exe","*\\msiexec.exe","*\\drvinst.exe","*\\wuauclt.exe","*\\System32\\svchost.exe") | search NOT user IN ("*$","SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, file_name, file_hash, proc_path
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
