File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54") or SHA1 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54") or MD5 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54") or SHA1 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54") or MD5 in~ ("b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b673b4e3400c71bd72464c98610c952e2164f70f946873b82adf3e6212851d54"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable Twig package (CVE-2026-46633) installed (twig/twig < 3.26.0) Exploitation High
Surface assets where Microsoft Defender TVM reports the Twig PHP templating library at a version vulnerable to CVE-2026-46633. Exploitation gives RCE via single-quote injection in a `{% use %}` template name; SecurityPolicy allows `{% use %}` even under sandbox, so any application that accepts attacker-influenced template names against twig/twig < 3.26.0 is reachable. Prioritise patching to 3.26.0 or later. Rationale: Article is a vendor advisory: identifies the exact package (composer:twig/twig), fixed version (3.26.0), and CVE (CVE-2026-46633). The only high-fidelity, non-generic detection from this content is asset coverage — every other behaviour-based UC (PHP web server spawning shells, web-shell cache file writes) collapses into generic web-shell rules already shipped, which the prompt explicitly excludes. [LLM] AWS IAM role trust policy created with set-qualified operator on GitHub OIDC sub claim Installation High
Hunts the exact misconfiguration class that @hulumi/policies <1.3.2 failed to flag: CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy CloudTrail events whose trust policy uses ForAnyValue:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringEquals against token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub. Any role created with this shape — particularly with wildcards in the sub value — is assumable by GitHub Actions workflows the role owner never intended to authorize. Rationale: Article specifies the exact unsafe pattern: set-qualified operators (ForAnyValue:StringLike etc.) applied to token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub bypass the inspector. CloudTrail's CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy carries the full policyDocument as JSON — substring matching for both the operator family AND the OIDC sub claim string is high-fidelity because the combination is essentially never seen in correctly-authored trust policies (canonical pattern is the bare StringLike or StringEquals). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition_operators.html • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services

[LLM] AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity from GitHub OIDC with unexpected repo/branch sub claim Exploitation Medium
Downstream hunt for actor abuse of a role whose unsafe trust policy slipped past @hulumi/policies <1.3.2. Pivots on sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events where the WebIdentity issuer is token.actions.githubusercontent.com and the asserted sub claim does not match the org's approved GitHub repo allowlist — flagging the first-time-seen repo+role pairs that an attacker exploiting a wildcard sub policy would generate. Rationale: The article's bypass directly enables GitHub Actions OIDC sub-claim impersonation against IAM roles. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is the actor-observable consequence — the userIdentity.userName field on the CloudTrail event carries the asserted sub (e.g. repo:owner/repo:ref:refs/heads/main). Anti-joining against an approved-org/repo lookup is the cleanest baseline-deviation pivot for catching exploitation of an unsafe policy that the scanner missed. Cross-referenced with the AWS GitHub OIDC docs and the Wiz misconfiguration write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services

[LLM] CVE-2026-46614: Unauthorized /fission-function/ invocation on Fission router public listener (port 8888) Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests to the internal-style /fission-function/<ns>/<name> route on the Fission router's public listener (svc/router, port 8888). On versions <= 1.22.0 this route is mounted on the public listener and allows any caller reaching the router to invoke any Function object — bypassing HTTPTrigger host/path/method restrictions. Post-fix (v1.23.0+), this path should only exist on port 8889 (svc/router-internal, ClusterIP-only), so any hit on port 8888 is either an unpatched cluster being exploited or an enumeration probe. Rationale: The path string `/fission-function/` and port 8888 are both directly named in the GHSA advisory as the vulnerable surface (pkg/router/httpTriggers.go:280-284 and svc/router listener config). After v1.23.0 this path should only appear on port 8889 (svc/router-internal), so hits on 8888 are unambiguous - either an exploitation attempt or an unpatched cluster still serving the route. We exclude 404 because that's enumeration covered by the next UC; 200 means successful unauthorized invocation, 502 means the function exists and went cold (still a successful enumeration). Defender KQL is empty because Fission runs on Linux K8s nodes and the relevant telemetry is HTTP-layer (ingress/WAF), not endpoint EDR. Falcon LogScale is empty for the same reason - FDR doesn't ship ingress HTTP path data. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Fission runs on Kubernetes (Linux) - this detection lives in ingress/WAF logs forwarded to CommonSecurityLog or web-tier IIS logs in front of the router
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | where DestinationPort == 8888 or isempty(tostring(DestinationPort))
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestClientApplication
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome has "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome has "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome has "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, DestinationIP=Computer, DestinationPort=sPort, RequestMethod=csMethod, RequestURL=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?",csUriQuery), "")), EventOutcome=tostring(scStatus), DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="IIS", RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome == "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome == "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome == "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
)
| where Verdict != "Probe miss"   // 200/502 = signal; 404 alone is enumeration noise covered by UC2
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Fission Router Unauthorized Function Invocation via /fission-function/ Path (CVE-2026-46614)
id: a7c4e9d2-3b8f-4c2a-91e7-fb7d6a8c1e3f
description: Detects HTTP requests to the /fission-function/<ns>/<name> path on the Fission router public listener (port 8888). On vulnerable versions (<= 1.22.0) this allows direct invocation of any Function without HTTPTrigger restrictions. Post-fix the path moved to internal port 8889 - so any hit on 8888 indicates exploitation or an unpatched cluster.

[LLM] Fission Function Name Enumeration via /fission-function/ Probing (CVE-2026-46614 recon) Reconnaissance Medium
Detects function-name discovery against the Fission router by counting distinct /fission-function/<ns>/<name> paths probed from the same source within a short window. Per the advisory, callers can enumerate which functions exist by differentiating response semantics (404 = no such function, 200 = invoked, 502 = function exists and went cold). A burst of 404s interleaved with 200/502s from one source is the canonical recon shape. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out enumeration as an impact: 'Enumerate function names by probing the response semantics (404 vs 200 vs 502 from cold start).' Counting distinct paths under /fission-function/ per source IP in a short window directly models that pattern; requiring at least 3 404s alongside the path-count threshold filters legitimate trigger callers (who hit known paths and don't miss). Sigma is empty because this is a count/threshold detection, not single-event-shape. Defender and Falcon are empty because the telemetry sits at the ingress/WAF layer, not on endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1595.003 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinUniquePaths = 5;
let MinProbeMisses = 3;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Router=DestinationIP
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, RequestURL=csUriStem, Status=tostring(scStatus), UserAgent=csUserAgent, Router=Computer
)
| summarize
    UniqueFunctionPaths = dcount(RequestURL),
    TotalRequests = count(),
    HitFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status in ("200","502")),
    MissFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status == "404"),
    SamplePaths = make_set(RequestURL, 20),
    UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5),
    Routers = make_set(Router, 3)
    by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes), SourceIP
| where UniqueFunctionPaths >= MinUniquePaths and MissFunctions >= MinProbeMisses
| extend EnumerationConfidence = case(
    HitFunctions > 0 and MissFunctions >= 3, "High - mixed 200/502 hits with 404 misses (likely successful enumeration)",
    MissFunctions >= 10, "Medium - heavy 404 probing",
    "Low")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] BadIIS rogue native module drop in IIS folders (demo.pdb / Chinese path heuristic) Installation Medium
Hunts non-trusted writes of DLL/native modules into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\), and image loads by w3wp.exe of modules outside the canonical IIS install paths or whose file path contains Han/CJK characters. Targets the Talos-described BadIIS commodity variant whose modules carry 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths inside IIS binaries as the Talos-recommended hunt hooks. Standard EDR can't search PDB strings inline, so we proxy with (a) writes of native modules into IIS paths by non-installer processes and (b) the CJK Unicode range (\u4e00-\u9fff) in module paths, which catches the Chinese-folder-path signal directly. Memory mem-1304 already corroborated BadIIS as commodity MaaS infrastructure.
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1036.005

| where FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".exe"

| where not(tolower(InitiatingProcessFileName) in (IISWriters))
| where FolderPath matches regex @"[\u4e00-\u9fff]" or not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite";
let ModuleLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName endswith ".dll"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"[\u4e00-\u9fff]"
   or (not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Program Files\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Program Files (x86)\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\assembly\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName="w3wp.exe", InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="ImageLoad";
union FileDrops, ModuleLoads
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Talos weekly prevalent-malware hash hit (Coinminer worm / TunMirror / SECOH-QAD / KMS-Loader) Installation High
Hash IOC sweep for the five Talos-published prevalent-malware SHA256s for the week ending May 21 2026: Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), PUA.Win.Tool.Tunmirror (TunMirror.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (SECOH-QAD.exe), and the KM-prefixed sample. Covers process execution, file writes, and DLL/EXE module loads to surface infection regardless of stage. Rationale: Direct hash IOCs published by Cisco Talos with detection name + sample filename per hash. These are the week's top prevalent samples — VID001.exe (Coinminer worm), TunMirror.exe (network tunneling PUA), SECOH-QAD.exe (KMS-emulation tooling), KM-prefix loader. Hash equality is the highest-fidelity detection shape possible. [LLM] BadIIS traffic-hijacking: IIS 503 surge + anomalous external redirect ratio per site/hour Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Talos-described BadIIS impact pattern: hijacked IIS servers throwing 503 spikes (proxy/upstream failure) while also emitting an unusually high ratio of 30x/redirect responses pointing visitors to attacker-controlled SEO-fraud destinations. Aggregates per site per hour and flags hours that materially deviate from the per-site baseline. Rationale: Article explicitly tells defenders to 'actively monitor IIS environments for unauthorized traffic redirection, unexpected reverse proxying, or sudden spikes in 503 Service Unavailable errors' — this query is a direct expression of that guidance, anchored on per-site/per-hour anomalies versus a 30-day baseline so it doesn't fire on legitimately redirect-heavy sites. Datadog and Falcon LogScale fields left empty because raw IIS W3C access logs are not part of the standard FDR feed and are not in the Datadog source list provided.
ATT&CKT1496 T1565.002 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let lookback = 7d;
let bucket = 1h;
let BadIISSignals = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where csMethod in~ ("GET","HEAD","POST")
| summarize Total = count(),
           Status503 = countif(scStatus == 503),
           Status3xx = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           DistinctClients = dcount(cIP),
           DistinctURIs = dcount(csUriStem),
           SampleUserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
           SampleReferers = make_set(csReferer, 5)
           by Computer, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, bucket)
| extend PctErr503 = round((Status503 * 100.0) / Total, 2),
         PctRedirect = round((Status3xx * 100.0) / Total, 2)
| where (Status503 >= 50 and PctErr503 >= 20) or (Status3xx >= 100 and PctRedirect >= 40);
let Baseline = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(lookback))
| summarize BaselineTotal = count(),
           BaselineRedirect = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           Baseline503 = countif(scStatus == 503)
           by Computer, sSiteName
| extend BaselinePctRedirect = round((BaselineRedirect * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2),
         BaselinePctErr503 = round((Baseline503 * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2);
BadIISSignals
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on Computer, sSiteName
| where PctRedirect >= (coalesce(BaselinePctRedirect, 0.0) * 3) or PctErr503 >= (coalesce(BaselinePctErr503, 0.0) * 3)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, Total, Status503, Status3xx, PctErr503, PctRedirect, BaselinePctRedirect, BaselinePctErr503, DistinctClients, DistinctURIs, SampleUserAgents, SampleReferers
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "d87e8d9d43758ce67a8052cb2334b99cc24f9b0437ee44815f360be0b22d835a", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "acd55c44b8b0d66d66defed85ca18082c092f048d3621da827fce593305c11fd", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "362498c3e71eeaa066a67e4a3f981d1c", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "0f03f72a92aef6d63eb74e73f8ac201d", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "d87e8d9d43758ce67a8052cb2334b99cc24f9b0437ee44815f360be0b22d835a", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "acd55c44b8b0d66d66defed85ca18082c092f048d3621da827fce593305c11fd", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "362498c3e71eeaa066a67e4a3f981d1c", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "0f03f72a92aef6d63eb74e73f8ac201d", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "d87e8d9d43758ce67a8052cb2334b99cc24f9b0437ee44815f360be0b22d835a", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "acd55c44b8b0d66d66defed85ca18082c092f048d3621da827fce593305c11fd", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "362498c3e71eeaa066a67e4a3f981d1c", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "0f03f72a92aef6d63eb74e73f8ac201d", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "d87e8d9d43758ce67a8052cb2334b99cc24f9b0437ee44815f360be0b22d835a", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "acd55c44b8b0d66d66defed85ca18082c092f048d3621da827fce593305c11fd", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "362498c3e71eeaa066a67e4a3f981d1c", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "0f03f72a92aef6d63eb74e73f8ac201d", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun Installation High
Detects an npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script (node.exe parented by npm) reaching out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases to download the Bun v1.3.13 runtime. This is the exact bootstrap behaviour of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 payload (bw_setup.js Stage-1) and is highly anomalous on developer endpoints because legitimate JS projects rarely pull Bun via a package-install hook. Rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/oven-sh/bun and Bun v1.3.13 as the runtime downloaded by Stage-1 bw_setup.js during npm preinstall — pairing the github.com/oven-sh/bun URL token with an npm-family parent process is a near-zero-FP signature on production endpoints (developer laptops will produce occasional FPs, hence the parent-process pinning). Cross-checked against Socket and Checkmarx advisories listed below. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
// Process-tree pivot — npm parent spawning a downloader child with Bun URL on the command line
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents)
    | where FileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FileName,
              ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Network pivot — same process families connecting to github.com for the Bun release tarball
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and (RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun" or RemoteUrl has "bun-windows" or RemoteUrl has "bun-linux" or RemoteUrl has "bun-darwin")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage   = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd     = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage  = "<network-egress>", ChildCmd = RemoteUrl, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256;
union ProcHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe","node","curl","wget","bun","bash","sh","pwsh"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren) or ParentProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren)
| where (ParentProcessName has_any (npmParents) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents))
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) Command & Control High
Detects any outbound network/DNS activity to the TeamPCP C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx (94.154.172.43) — particularly POSTs to the /v1/telemetry path — that exfiltrates harvested cloud, CI/CD and developer credentials from compromised hosts. The domain visually impersonates Checkmarx's legitimate infrastructure but resolves to attacker-controlled space. Rationale: Article Table 1 names the C2 server, IP and HTTP path explicitly (audit.checkmarx[.]cx:443 / 94.154.172.43 / /v1/telemetry) — any hit on these three indicators is a confirmed-compromise signal, not a hunting hypothesis. Corroborated by Checkmarx's official disclosure that all four artifact families (npm, Docker Hub, GitHub Actions, VS Code) shared this C2. Cross-checked against: • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "audit.checkmarx[.]cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2Hosts)) or (RemoteIP in (c2Ips)) or (RemoteUrl has c2Path and RemotePort in (443, 80))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (c2Hosts) or DstIpAddr in (c2Ips) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has c2Path and DstPortNumber in (443, 80))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Hosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseCodeName
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or Url has c2Path and (HttpHostName has "checkmarx.cx")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or DestinationIP in (c2Ips) or RequestURL has "audit.checkmarx.cx" or RequestURL has c2Path
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers) Installation High
Detects creation or execution of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) and Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js scripts dropped by the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package, as well as the 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' string written into public repo content that the worm uses as an attribution marker and propagation beacon. This catches both the install-time drop on the npm install path and any post-compromise replay. Rationale: Article explicitly names bw_setup.js (Stage-1 bootstrap, registered as the `bw` bin) and bw1.js (Stage-2 Bun payload) inside the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 package. The legitimate Bitwarden CLI ships neither filename, so the filename + package path combo is a hard-IOC match. The Shai-Hulud Third Coming string is a TeamPCP attribution marker per the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes

let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let shaiHuludMarker = "Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (FolderPath has_any (packageHints) and FileName endswith ".js") or (AdditionalFields has shaiHuludMarker)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName = FileName, SHA256, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);

let npmRunners = dynamic(["npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (TargetFilePath has_any (packageHints) and TargetFileExtension =~ "js")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (npmRunners) or ParentProcessName has_any (npmRunners)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,

union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Outdated Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 · [LLM] Symbolic-link / junction creation from low-IL context targeting SAM hive or Defender scan dirs (CVE-2026-41091) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor

[LLM] Outdated Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 Exploitation High
Hunts the estate for endpoints still running a Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform below the fixed builds (1.1.26040.8 / 4.18.26040.7) where CVE-2026-41091 (link-following SYSTEM EoP) and CVE-2026-45498 (DoS) are exploitable. Article-specific because it pivots on the exact CVE IDs Microsoft and CISA added to KEV on 21 May 2026 with a 3 June 2026 remediation deadline. Rationale: Pivots on the exact two CVEs Microsoft disclosed as actively exploited (article body) and CISA's 3 June 2026 KEV deadline. Cross-checked against DailyCVE write-up that confirms the fixed engine version 1.1.26040.8 and the link-following primitive against SAM. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/

[LLM] Symbolic-link / junction creation from low-IL context targeting SAM hive or Defender scan dirs (CVE-2026-41091) Exploitation High
Detects the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091: a non-elevated user invokes mklink, fsutil reparsepoint, or PowerShell New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink/Junction with a path pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or at the Defender Scans/Platform/Quarantine directories. Defender's scan engine (SYSTEM) then follows the link and reads/writes the protected file. Article-specific via the CWE-59 link-following mechanic confirmed in the DailyCVE write-up. Rationale: Pivots on the CWE-59 link-following primitive disclosed for CVE-2026-41091 — symlink in a Defender-scanned location pointing at a SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hive. The combination of low-IL parent + link-creation binary + sensitive target path is high-fidelity: legitimate symlinks to those hive files from non-admin context are essentially non-existent. DailyCVE write-up confirmed the SAM exploitation path. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/
ATT&CKT1068 T1574 T1003.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "mklink")
   or (FileName =~ "fsutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "reparsepoint" and ProcessCommandLine has "set")
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "New-Item" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SymbolicLink","Junction"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("System","High")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe" and CommandLine has "mklink")
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\fsutil.exe" and CommandLine has "reparsepoint" and CommandLine has "set")
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "New-Item" and (CommandLine has "SymbolicLink" or CommandLine has "Junction"))
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where TokenElevationType != "%%1937"  // 1937 = full elevated; we want low-IL exploit attempts
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, LogonId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Symbolic Link or Junction Creation Targeting SAM Hive or Defender Scan Dir (CVE-2026-41091)
id: 7a2c9b5e-3f48-4d11-9c64-2bb7a9d5e1a0
description: Detects creation of a symbolic link, junction, or reparse point from a low-integrity user context pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or Microsoft Defender scan/platform/quarantine directories. This is the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091 (link following in Microsoft Defender allowing SYSTEM elevation).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-warns-of-two-actively.html
  - https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1574
  - attack.t1003.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_mklink:
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'mklink'
  selection_fsutil:
    Image|endswith: '\fsutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'reparsepoint'
      - 'set'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'New-Item'
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - 'SymbolicLink'
      - 'Junction'
  target_paths:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '\System32\config\SAM'
      - '\System32\config\SYSTEM'
      - '\System32\config\SECURITY'
      - 'Windows Defender\Scans'
      - 'Windows Defender\Platform'
      - 'Windows Defender\Quarantine'
  condition: (selection_mklink or selection_fsutil or selection_ps) and target_paths
falsepositives:
  - Sysadmin manual hive backups using fsutil to inspect reparse points
  - Legitimate IT scripts maintaining Defender exclusion junctions in vendor-approved scenarios
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\\cmd.exe OR @Image:*\\fsutil.exe OR @Image:*\\powershell.exe OR @Image:*\\pwsh.exe OR @Image:*\\PowerShell.exe) (@CommandLine:*mklink* OR @CommandLine:*reparsepoint* OR @CommandLine:*SymbolicLink* OR @CommandLine:*Junction*) (@CommandLine:*config\\SAM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SYSTEM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SECURITY* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Scans* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Platform* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Quarantine*) -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|fsutil|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(mklink|reparsepoint\s+set|New-Item.*(SymbolicLink|Junction))/i
| CommandLine=/(System32\\config\\(SAM|SYSTEM|SECURITY)|Windows\s+Defender\\(Scans|Platform|Quarantine))/i
| IntegrityLevel!=/^(System|High)$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| where process_integrity_level!="system" AND process_integrity_level!="high"
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-41091", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-42897", "CVE-2010-0806", "CVE-2010-0249", "CVE-2009-1537", "CVE-2008-4250", "CVE-2009-3459")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
